name: main
final_message:
I recorded 22 papers and wrote the review. That is below the 25–40 target. Only 4 papers were read from PDF pages. Of the rest, 3 were read through Europe PMC text and 15 are abstract-only.

**Our dataset.** It is confirmed as Lumpe & Stanković (PNAS 2021). Labels come from periodic Euler–Bernoulli beam finite-element homogenization of circular struts, with Es = 1 MPa and nu_s = 0.3. Every structure is at rho_rel = 0.01, so your 1% inference is right and the scatter is the rounding of C and n. The PNAS PDF would not load in `read_pdf`, so I read its Methods through Europe PMC. That text has no page numbers, and the supplementary information was not read.

**Most relevant papers**
1. **Grega et al. 2024 (ICLR):** the MACE-based equivariant GNN with a positive semi-definite output layer, built on a Lumpe-derived dataset (8,954 lattices after cleaning, plus node perturbations). Without that layer, 30% of lattices got negative eigenvalues. Their L_comp errors are not in log10 units, so they are not a baseline for us.
2. **Indurkar et al. 2022:** a message-passing GNN with periodic edges on this same catalog (17,201 lattices). It classifies stretching vs bending (81.8% validation accuracy on a random split) and independently confirms rho = 0.01 and the E = Es·C·rho^n form.
3. **Bastek 2022 and Zheng 2023:** precedents for predicting the 9 orthotropic constants, with different data, densities and beam models. They are not baselines for us.

**Gaps I could not fill**
- **Catalog counts:** four numbers are in play and I could not reconcile them: 17,087 in the paper, 17,201 in Indurkar, 17,221 and 17,262 in ours.
- **The 41 small-member lattices:** the paper only says they were excluded for numerical issues. I found nothing else about how they were handled.
- **How C and n were fitted:** the paper defers this to the supplementary information, which I did not read. It also leaves open whether node volumes are corrected in relative density.
- **Baselines:** no published log10-modulus errors exist on this catalog, so you will need your own baselines.
- **Defects:** the defect papers were abstract-only, so I have no knockdown numbers. I found no ML model of stiffness under strut waviness, diameter variation, missing struts or porosity. The only published setup I found is the node-perturbation FE dataset in Grega 2024 (nodal perturbation only).
- **Not read:** Dallago 2019 was not read or recorded, and the JMPS companion to Grega 2024 is abstract-only.

The review has a correction note on Section 5. Meyer 2024, Frey 2025 and Zheng 2023 surfaced in searches, but I did not confirm they use this catalog.
